messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Jarvis is fully up to date, James: it restarted at 4:59 PM, after the last build. The name fix is live, so tap my name on your phone, then type your message, and it should arrive as one line.

messages.name: James
messages.text: I don’t wanna add more noise to work it out and need a good place to feed my input to

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Use your private Jarvis chat as the one place for all your input, James. Click Jarvis at the top of the strip and just dump thoughts there: ideas, bugs, "fix this later". The team doesn't see it, so it adds no noise, and Jarvis puts each item on the to-do list and offers to hand it to a teammate when you're ready. On your phone the private chat isn't there yet, so start messages with "Jarvis," in the team chat. If you want, I can bring the private chat to the iPhone later.

messages.name: James
messages.text: Let's do it

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: On it. This one's taking a minute.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: The Mac half of the private chat on the iPhone is done, James. The phone screen itself still needs building, and it's in the iPhone app's folder, which Jarvis has to hand me. - **Done on the Mac:** the Mac now accepts private messages for Jarvis from the phone, both at home and away, using the same conversation as the Mac's Jarvis tab. It also sends the private chat, Jarvis's answer buttons and a "thinking" signal back to the phone.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: The build worked, and it takes effect after a "Restart Jarvis". - **Still to do on the phone:** a Jarvis tab in the iPhone app, plus the earlier phone fixes (tapping a name should start your message, and missing messages). To get that started, say in your private Jarvis chat: "Hand Claude Code the iPhone Jarvis tab and phone message fixes".

messages.name: James
messages.text: Restart Jarvis

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Restart done, James: Jarvis is running everything from today, including the Mac half of private chat on the phone. The iPhone side is next whenever Jarvis hands it to me.

messages.name: James
messages.text: Hand it over

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: That message came to me, James, but the handoff has to come from Jarvis, and I can't start the iPhone work from here. In the Jarvis tab of the chat box, send exactly: "Hand Claude Code the iPhone app: Jarvis tab, name-tap fix, missing messages". Jarvis will ask "Hand this to Claude Code?"; tap "Hand it off" and I'll start right away.

messages.name: James
messages.text: Also I can’t see the Mac app now

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Still working. I'll read that as soon as I finish.

messages.name: James
messages.text: It’s there

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: On it. This one's taking a minute.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Jarvis is running, James, and the strip is on the screen: at the right edge, near the middle, 150 points wide. I can't take a screenshot to see what it looks like. Since it now opens with just Jarvis, there may be only one small row there. Try this: click J in the menu bar and choose "Show or Hide Jarvis" twice. If you still see nothing, choose Look, then Studio, which has a solid background.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Still working. I'll read that as soon as I finish.

messages.name: James
messages.text: But we need something to make it easier on the layer with everything behind

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: On it. This one's taking a minute.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: The strip is now easier to see over busy windows, James. Jarvis and each teammate now sit on their own frosted card, dark in Workspace and light in Studio, instead of floating with no background. Jarvis's card has a blue edge, and a teammate who's done gets a green one. The build worked, but I couldn't look at it on your screen. It shows after a "Restart Jarvis".

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Still working. I'll read that as soon as I finish.

messages.name: Jarvis
messages.text: Handed to Claude Code: Convert Jarvis to Grok bot. I'll tell you when it's done.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: On it: Convert Jarvis to Grok bot.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: Done: Jarvis is now a standing Grok bot, set up as a Grok agent profile (`jarvis-agent.md`) that keeps one ongoing conversation, so it remembers what you told it earlier in the day. It starts a fresh conversation each day or after 40 messages. The app builds, and in a test outside the app it answered "where are things at?" from the live team status and later remembered your dentist time. That test showed it adding the dentist to the team to-do list, so I told it to keep personal notes off the list; I haven't re-tested that change, and the real app hasn't run the new code yet.

messages.name: Claude Code
messages.text: You don't need to do anything once Jarvis restarts the app, then just talk to Jarvis as usual.

messages.name: Jarvis
messages.text: Handed to Gemini: Clean public chat copy. I'll tell you when it's done.

messages.name: Gemini
messages.text: On it: Clean public chat copy.

messages.name: Gemini
messages.text: Done: Here is the cleaned public chat copy for the Jarvis apps under `~/Documents/AgentBand`, with James's personal phone number removed and the 14:35 Grok line rewritten:  ***  **[14:15] Jarvis:** Good afternoon, team. James has approved the staging site migration for the web app. Claude Code, you're clear to proceed with the build. Codex, standby to assist with Apple TV API integration once Claude finishes.  **[14:18] Claude Code:** On it. Pulling the latest branch from GitHub now. Should have a preview build ready in 20 minutes.

messages.name: Gemini
messages.text: **[14:22] Gemini:** Copy updates for the homepage and onboarding flow are finalized and pushed to the repository. Let me know if any microcopy needs tweaking during the build.  **[14:25] Codex:** Standing by for the Apple TV build. Apple Silicon local build passed successfully.  **[14:30] Grok:** Quick lookup: Swift 6 concurrency warnings on the new TVOS target are down to zero after the latest header cleanups. Smooth sailing ahead.  **[14:32] Jarvis:** Excellent updates. James is currently heads-down on product review; keep me posted here if any blockers pop up.

messages.name: Gemini
messages.text: **[14:35] Grok:** Research note: Checked the latest Apple HIG guidelines for widget refresh rates—we are well within limits, no battery drain concerns for the edge strip.  ***  **Summary for James:**  Cleaned the public chat copy to remove your phone number and rewrote Grok's 14:35 line to focus on widget research instead. No further action needed on your end; ready for Claude Code to drop in.
